title: CI route for a macOS-built, signed darwin artifact: release.yml publishes a Mac-signed asset (follow-up of WCLI-96)
description: DEC-255 (opum-doc): for the 0.1.1 release the publish route is the operator sitting on minim4 (build, ad-hoc sign, codesign --verify --strict as the gate, upload with gh release upload --clobber). This task is the CI-route follow-up: release.yml must take a macOS-built, ad-hoc-signed artifact so a CI-driven release can publish. REQUIRED before any CI-driven release after the public flip; it does not gate the 0.1.1 release. Measured 2026-11-01 on minim4 (macOS 27.0.1, arm64, bun 1.3.14, dev 5bf5ec8): a plain macOS bun build fails codesign --verify --strict (invalid signature; flags adhoc,linker-signed, 15574 hashes) and codesign -s - --force on a copy verifies (valid on disk; flags adhoc, 3894+2 hashes) and runs; the sha256 and cdhash change with the re-sign. Open: the macOS runner, which is billed and so needs the operator spend decision (dec-14tajwo was answered B for now) or a Mac runner of ours (a security-posture change), the cdhash source in the release notes (scripts/macho-cdhash.mjs on the re-signed bytes: measured on 2026-11-01, it equals codesign -dvvv CDHash= on a re-signed copy, test/release-metadata.test.ts), and the runbook byte comparison, superseded for 0.1.1.

acceptanceCriteria.text: release.yml publishes only an artifact that was built and ad-hoc signed on macOS and that passed codesign --verify --strict in the same run
The release notes carry the sha256 and cdhash of the signed bytes, and the published checksum is regenerated from them
The runbook describes the CI route and no longer carries the superseded runner-vs-Mac comparison
An independent Opus review covers the release-path change, and the operator decides the macOS runner question

implementationNotes: Dependency, per the #232 review: build and release also run on the self-hosted Linux runner, which has no runner after the public flip. WCLI-99 moves both to hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm, so this task depends on WCLI-99 landing; the macOS runner for a CI-built signed artifact is the separate, operator-owned question recorded in this task. Until this task lands, the release route is the operator sitting and scripts/regenerate-release-metadata.mjs (docs/runbooks/publish-a-mac-signed-ward-release-asset.md).

Correction (round-3 finding 3 on opum-ai/ward-cli#232): the earlier note says WCLI-99 moves build and release to hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm. That is now true: opum-ai/ward-cli#237 (WCLI-99) merged on dev and takes ci.yml and release.yml build and release to unconditional hosted ubuntu-24.04-arm. WCLI-99 as originally filed covered pull_request jobs only; its record gains a note naming this scope. The dependency is recorded structurally.
